Cāṅgadeva
------------------------------------------
Cāṅgadeva was a saint from Maha-rashtra who was a contemporary of the famous Sant Jñāneśvar (13th cent. A.D.). He was a haṭhayogi with several miraculous powers and a host of disciples. Having heard of the great fame of Sant Jñāneśvar he wanted to humiliate him by making a show of his power. He once flew through the air riding on a fierce tiger. Jñāneśvar who was then sitting on a mud wall, along with his brother Sopāna and sister Muktā-bāī, commanded the wall to fly and it did, carrying them all, much to the chagrin of the haṭhayogi! चाङ्गदेव surrendered. At the instance of Jñāneśvar, his younger sister मुक्ताबाई initiated चाङ्गदेव into the mysteries of ज्ञानयोग. He became one of their most devoted disciples and has composed quite a few अभङ्गस् in which he has described some of his mystic experiences got by their grace.
There is another चाङ्गदेव who was a grandson of the great mathematician भास्कराचार्य (A. D. 1114-1160). He was the chief astrologer under Siṅghana (a Yādava king) and founded a college for the study of सिद्धान्त-śiromaṇi, भास्कर’s magnum opus.
See also ABHAṄGAS.
